ai.definition: Coal power involves burning pulverized coal in a boiler to generate steam, which then drives turbines to produce electricity.
ai.howItWorks: Coal is crushed into fine particles and burned in a furnace. The heat from the combustion raises water to high-pressure steam, which is directed through pipes to drive turbine blades, converting thermal energy into mechanical energy that generates electricity.
ai.problemSolved: Historically provided reliable baseload power with established infrastructure.
ai.manufacturing: Coal mines extract and process coal for use in power plants. Power plant construction involves building boilers, turbines, and associated equipment.
ai.buildProcess: Mining operations extract raw coal, which is transported to the power plant where it undergoes processing before being burned in a boiler.
ai.costDrivers: Costs include mining, transportation, fuel storage, and environmental compliance. Operational costs are driven by maintenance and labor expenses.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Facing increasing competition from renewable sources due to environmental regulations and cost pressures; however, still used in some regions for baseload power.
ai.regulation: Subject to various emissions standards and carbon pricing policies. Regulations are becoming stricter, driving costs up and reducing demand.
ai.risks: Environmental risks include air pollution and water contamination. Economic risks arise from rising fuel prices and regulatory pressures.
ai.profitability: Profit margins have declined due to increased operational costs and competition from renewables. However, some regions still see profitability in coal power plants.
ai.futureDevelopment: Investments are shifting towards cleaner technologies such as carbon capture and storage (CCS) to reduce emissions, but this technology is not yet widely adopted.

glossary.def: Fine particles of coal that are burned in a boiler to produce steam.
A type of electricity supply that provides constant, reliable energy demand over long periods.

subsystems.name: Fuel handling and preparation
subsystems.role: stores, crushes and dries coal into a fine powder so it burns like a gas.

subsystems.name: Boiler and furnace
subsystems.role: burns pulverised coal to raise high-pressure, high-temperature steam.

subsystems.name: Steam turbine and generator
subsystems.role: expands steam through turbines to spin a generator and produce electricity.

subsystems.name: Cooling and water system
subsystems.role: condenses exhaust steam and rejects waste heat to the environment.

subsystems.name: Emissions control
subsystems.role: removes particulates, sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from flue gas.

subsystems.name: Ash and byproduct handling
subsystems.role: collects and disposes of or reuses bottom ash and fly ash.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the site
buildSteps.detail: Clear and level land, build foundations for the boiler, turbine hall and cooling towers, and provide rail or road access for coal delivery.

buildSteps.title: Erect the boiler
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the tall steel frame and weld the water-wall tubes, superheater and economiser into the furnace structure.

buildSteps.title: Install the turbine and generator
buildSteps.detail: Place the multi-stage steam turbine and the generator on a common shaft, aligned to fractions of a millimetre.

buildSteps.title: Build the cooling system
buildSteps.detail: Construct cooling towers or intake and outfall channels for once-through cooling, and install circulating water pumps.

buildSteps.title: Add emissions controls
buildSteps.detail: Install electrostatic precipitators or fabric filters, flue-gas desulphurisation scrubbers and selective catalytic reduction units in the flue-gas path.

buildSteps.title: Wire and instrument
buildSteps.detail: Connect the generator to the grid via transformers and switchgear, and install the distributed control system and sensors.

buildSteps.title: Commission and test
buildSteps.detail: Fire the boiler on oil or gas, then coal; raise steam, roll the turbine, synchronise to the grid and tune combustion and emissions.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Run as baseload or load-following plant, with regular inspection of boiler tubes, turbine blades and emissions equipment.

prerequisites.why: grinding coal to talcum-powder fineness allows rapid, complete burning in a compact furnace.
converts steam at hundreds of degrees Celsius and pressures above 200 bar into rotary power.
superheater and turbine components must resist creep and oxidation at 600 °C and above.
modern air-quality rules require removal of over 99% of particulates and most sulphur and nitrogen oxides.

pathway.milestone: existing plants run as legacy baseload, with retirements accelerating in many regions
pathway.unlocks: short-term grid reliability while replacements are built.

pathway.milestone: co-firing biomass or ammonia in some boilers to cut net carbon emissions
pathway.unlocks: a transitional use of existing coal assets with lower emissions.

pathway.milestone: carbon capture and storage retrofits on a limited number of plants
pathway.unlocks: a possible lifeline for otherwise stranded coal capacity, if costs and transport networks allow.

pathway.milestone: phase-out or repurposing of coal sites for synchronous condensers, grid storage or renewable hubs
pathway.unlocks: reuse of grid connections and land as coal-fired generation ends.
